messages:
josef-customer: Hey team — after the scheduled cert rotation for our private gateway (gw-prod-1) we started getting 502s from our service. We used the rotator upload flow and the bundle claimed success, but many clients report TLS handshake errors: 'tls: handshake error: remote error: unknown authority'. Anyone seen this after a rotation?

sara-support: Sorry you're hitting this, tagging infra. Can you paste the haproxy/nginx error and the cert chain from an `openssl s_client` result? Also confirm whether this gateway sits behind a NAT/egress allowlist. :ear

matt-eng: Likely an incomplete chain or AIA fetch blocked by egress rules. Quick checks you can run from a host that reaches gw-prod-1: 
```
# show what the server is presenting
openssl s_client -connect gw-prod-1.private.example:443 -showcerts -servername gw.prod.internal
```
And from the gateway host check whether it can fetch the issuing intermediate: 
```
curl -vS https://acme-ca.example.org/intermediates/42.pem -o /tmp/intermediate.pem
```

josef-customer: Paste of openssl output (sanitized):
```
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=0 CN = gw.prod.internal
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=gw.prod.internal
   i:/CN=Our Intermediate CA (sha256)
---
```
And haproxy log: `Apr 03 15:11:54 gw-prod-1 haproxy[1220]: Server backend/app-1 SSL handshake failure, no certificate presented by server`

linh-support: That `unable to get local issuer certificate` + only a single cert in chain means the gateway is serving only the leaf. Two common causes for private deployments: (1) the rotator upload omitted intermediates (bundle parsing error), or (2) the gateway attempted to fetch AIA/intermediate URLs during rotation but egress/firewall blocked the fetch so the system fell back to installing just the leaf.

infra-oncall: Can you run these from inside the VPC where rotator runs / on the gateway: 
```
# check DNS resolution for AIA/OCSP endpoints
dig +short acme-ca.example.org
# check tcp/connect to port 443 from gateway host
curl -I https://acme-ca.example.org/status || true
# try fetching intermediate explicitly
curl -sv https://acme-ca.example.org/intermediates/42.pem -o -
```
If the curl hangs or times out => egress blocked. If it returns 403/404 => issuer endpoint issue.

matt-eng: Also check the rotator upload type. If you used the `leaf_only` option accidentally, the rotator will not include intermediates even if available. We have a rotator-bot message in the audit log showing upload metadata.

rotator-bot: Rotator upload event: user=josef-customer bucket=rotator-uploads/gw-prod-1 object=2026-03-17-rot-2156789000 bundle_type=leaf_only status=200

josef-customer: Ah — we did a quick automation change and apparently switched to leaf-only. But our automation runs inside a VPC with strict egress allowlist; I still want to confirm whether the rotator would have fetched the intermediate if allowed.

linh-support: If rotator had `bundle_type=full_chain` it attempts to fetch missing intermediates from AIA/OCSP during processing. Two remediation paths: 
1) Short term: re-upload a full chain bundle (leaf + intermediates + root) manually via the console or API. That avoids any AIA fetches.
2) Longer term: allow egress to the issuer endpoints so rotator can fetch automatically. Add `acme-ca.example.org` and the OCSP hostnames to your egress allowlist / NAT gateway policy.

matt-eng: Repro steps for you to validate locally before reupload: 
```
# simulate client check showing missing intermediate
openssl s_client -connect gw-prod-1.private.example:443 -showcerts -CAfile /etc/ssl/certs/ca-bundle.crt
# now test a reupload with combined bundle (leaf + intermediate)
# create bundle.pem with leaf then intermediate then root
cat leaf.pem intermediate.pem root.pem > full_chain.pem
# POST to rotator API (example)
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ 
  -F "bundle=@full_chain.pem" https://console.redwood.ai/api/v1/rotator/upload?gateway=gw-prod-1
```

josef-customer: Trying reupload now with full chain. Also opening ticket with our network team to allowlist the issuer hosts.

sara-support: Great — after you reupload, restart the gateway service (haproxy/nginx) or trigger a config reload so it picks up the new cert. Let us know the `openssl s_client` result after. :thumbsup:

josef-customer: Reupload done and reload triggered. `openssl s_client` now shows two certs in chain and verify OK: `Verify return code: 0 (ok)`. Traffic looks normal again, 502s dropped to zero. Thanks for the fast help.

infra-oncall: For postmortem: recommend adding a pre-rotation check that validates the uploaded bundle contains intermediate certificates (simple parse) and/or runs an outbound fetch test for known issuer hosts when `bundle_type=full_chain` is selected. Filing an internal infra ticket to add that check.

josef-customer: Confirmed fix. We'll also update our automation to default to `full_chain` and request egress allowlist updates. Appreciated! :raised_hands:
